newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to ease back to 4,325 from 4,355.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to ease back to 4,325 from 4,355.

text.p: A positive start in the London stock market on Wednesday may be eroded as the day progresses and this will make FTSE 100 index ease back to around 4,325 after reaching 4,355, technical analysts said.
By 0816 GMT, at the pre-market open, the FTSE was indicated up 2.3 at 4,347.0.

Its clumsy movements since last week -- when it bolted to an intra-day high of 4,362.4 only to turn back in desperation to 4,312.4 serves to highlight investor nervousness and the startling way in which the index can change gear without notice, they added.

Individual stock within the index -- such as those within the banking or retailing sectors -- can also come in and out of favour very quickly and this stop-go action merely slows the market down and leaves it hobbling within a restricted range, analysts said.
Wall Street appeared less defensive yesterday -- the Dow closed up 30.01 to 7,038.21 -- and in theory this should help the FTSE to go higher in early trading today.
But the chances of it stretching to new highs and staying there are likely to be squandered and the FTSE will drift back to a more comfortable position near 4,325.
